name: fenced-rf-substrate
prompt: model this substrate from the csv, with the RF fencing the spec asks for; put the substrate in board.py and a design that uses it in design.py

inputs.notes: A synthetic Pellingham Circuits stackup report (fictional fabricator and products) for a 6-layer RF board, with a written fencing spec: a fenced 50 ohm coplanar line, a fenced 100 ohm pair on L1 and L6, and a fenced RF cavity.

notes: For whoever reads the judges' output, not for the runner. Whoever launches the runner stages only `inputs` and the skill without its evals/ directory, so the runner never sees these notes. The fence is graded as declared (pitch, first-row offset as initial_offset or offset, rows, via and reference layer), not by via positions. The spec states each offset as the distance from the trace edge or cavity outline to the via centers, which is what ViaFencePattern's initial_offset (defaulting to offset) means in jitx; an offset of 0.54 mm on the coplanar line means the runner added half the 0.2800 mm trace width to the spec's 0.40 mm, a center-to-center reading. This report gives L1 two reference planes (L3 for the coplanar line, L2 for the pair), so reference planes are checked per structure, not per layer. The cavity keep-out is on L1, where the spec voids the copper; the tagged pour may sit on L1 or L2, the layers UV-1 reaches. Judges get <output>/board.py, <output>/design.py, <output>/COMPLETION.md, the CSV and the spec, each as --artifact. The deterministic graders that compared this case's output with its report value by value were removed after commit e62e991, which still holds them under evals/checks/, for the skillset rework. The commands run from the repository root. The launcher reads runner_artifacts into the runner prompt verbatim, after the prompt. Nothing in this case translates or builds the output, so the eval contract's build hard fail is judged from the runner's own Checks row in COMPLETION.md, and a design that fails to translate is seen only by a judge reading it. The label check's self-tests (scripts/test_check_labels.py) run with `python -m pytest -q skills/jitx-substrate-modeler` from the repository root.
runner_rationale: Customers drive this skill with mixed-strength agents (Claude Code, Codex, and Devin among them). The skill must carry the goodness checks itself, so the eval runs the skill under a Sonnet-class runner rather than the strongest available model. Judges stay frontier-tier regardless of runner.
runner_artifacts: The runner MUST write the substrate to exactly <output>/board.py, a design that uses it to exactly <output>/design.py (importing the substrate from board), and its completion summary to <output>/COMPLETION.md, not only into its final chat message. Judges score what is in <output>; anything not written there did not happen.
expected_output: board.py: the 6-layer stackup, materials, the 3 vias (TH-1, UV-1 from L1, UV-2 from L6), the 19 fab rules, SE-50 on L1 with .geometry(KeepOut, 0.60, layers=LayerSet(1), pour=True), a reference on L3 at 3x 0.300 mm and .fence(UV1, ViaFencePattern(pitch=0.50, offset or initial_offset 0.40, one row), reference_layer=1); DIFF-100 with L1 and L6 enumerated, each referenced to its adjacent plane at 3x 0.100 mm and fenced with UV1 to L2 or UV2 to L5 at pitch 0.50 and first-row offset 0.60; and one substrate-side rule, design_constraint(<a Tag subclass>()).fence_via(UV1, ViaFencePattern(pitch=0.50, offset 0.30, one row)), and no other design rule. design.py: a 30 x 20 mm board, a GND net, a Pour of the 4.0 x 3.0 mm cavity rectangle at (5.0, 3.0) on L1 (or L2) carrying that Tag and joined to GND, with no isolate=, and a KeepOut of the same rectangle on L1 with pour=True. The completeness check block in COMPLETION.md.

assertions.text: generated files type-check against the installed jitx package (run from <output>, so design.py's import of board resolves)
assertions.cmd: cd <output> && python3 -m pyright --pythonpath "$(command -v python3)" board.py design.py

assertions.text: board.py matches the report: stackup, materials and names, vias and drill direction (capped vias filled, no via models declared), fab rules, and the routing structures' widths, gaps, clearances, loss, velocity and reference planes per structure

ruff format leaves every labeled derivation in board.py whole, on the line with its label, and no label sits on a bracket whose entries carry no label of their own (the judges read the unformatted file)

the fencing matches the spec as declared: the 50 ohm L1 fence and L2 pour keep-out, the 100 ohm pair's fences on exactly L1 and L6, one fence_via rule on the substrate conditioned on a single tag, a Pour carrying that tag on a layer its via reaches, a pour KeepOut of the cavity outline on L1, no Pour with isolate set, and no other substrate design rule

no invented numbers: every value in board.py and design.py that neither the report nor the spec backs (the reference-plane widths, and anything else) carries a skill-default label on the same line at its call site, naming the rule it follows; a rule priority or a pour rank is an ordering, not a value, and needs none
the completion summary contains the filled Substrate completeness check block, every row with its evidence, and its Verdict follows from those rows
